[LTIM.4.3.3] `add_months` and `add_years` on a `Time` shift the calendar
date in UTC and preserve the UTC time-of-day: the instant's UTC calendar
date moves by the given months or years, clamping per [LTIM.4.3.2], and
the nanoseconds since that date's midnight are kept. A `Time` stores no
zone ([LTIM.1.1.3]), so there is no original offset to preserve. An author
who needs the shift on a zone's calendar takes the date in that zone
([LTIM.6.5]), shifts the `Date`, and reads the instant back from it.

A shift whose result its type cannot represent, a `Time` outside the range of
[LTIM.1.1.5] or a `Date` outside the range of [LTIM.1.2.2], raises a
`ComputationError` of kind `NOT_REPRESENTABLE` ([LERR.1.4.10]).
